sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**

AXISBANK's latest annual report reveals a complex financial landscape, with various subsidiaries and associate companies contributing to its overall performance. As of 31 March 2025, the bank's consolidated net assets stood at ₹150,235 crore, with a profit of ₹24,861.43 crore for the year ended 31 March 2024. The bank's revenue recognition policies are in accordance with AS-9 and RBI guidelines, with interest income recognized on an accrual basis. The bank also has a significant provision for contingent liabilities, with ₹904.76 crore held towards claims assessed as probable as of 31 March 2025.

**Investment Thesis**

Our investment thesis for AXISBANK is centered on its ability to navigate the complexities of the Indian banking landscape while maintaining a strong financial position. With a significant presence in the market and a diverse range of subsidiaries and associate companies, AXISBANK is well-positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities. However, the bank's high provision for contingent liabilities and employee benefits expenses, which stood at ₹288.99 crore for the year ended 31 March 2025, may pose a risk to its profitability. Nevertheless, with a strong net asset base and a proven track record of performance, we believe that AXISBANK is an attractive investment opportunity for those seeking exposure to the Indian banking sector.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body: Axis Bank is a private sector bank in India that provides a complete suite of banking products and financial services covering retail banking, wholesale banking, and treasury operations. As of 31 March, 2025, the Bank's total assets were ₹1,609,930 crores [Standalone], with total deposits of ₹1,172,952 crores [Standalone] and total advances of ₹1,040,811 crores [Standalone]. The Bank's operating revenue increased by 10% year-on-year to ₹79,605 crores [Standalone] in fiscal 2025, with a net interest income of ₹54,348 crores [Standalone] and non-interest income of ₹25,257 crores [Standalone]. The Bank's segmental results for fiscal 2025 show that the Retail Banking segment had a total segment revenue of ₹76,044.88 crores [Standalone], while the Corporate/Wholesale Banking segment had a total segment revenue of ₹38,132.43 crores [Standalone], and the Treasury segment had a total segment revenue of ₹28,666.56 crores [Standalone]. The Other Banking Business segment had a total segment revenue of ₹52,913.53 crores [Standalone].

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body: The financial performance of AXISBANK for the fiscal year 2025 has been notable, with operating revenue increasing by 10% year-on-year to ₹79,605 crores [Standalone]. Net Interest Income (NII) grew 9% to ₹54,348 crores [Standalone], while non-interest income rose 13% to ₹25,257 crores [Standalone]. Operating expenses increased 6% to ₹37,500 crores [Standalone], resulting in an operating profit growth of 13% to ₹42,105 crores [Standalone]. Provisions and contingencies saw a significant increase of 91% to ₹7,759 crores [Standalone], leading to a net profit growth of 6% to ₹26,373 crores [Standalone]. The bank's total assets expanded from ₹1,477,209 crores as of March 31, 2024, to ₹1,609,930 crores as of March 31, 2025, with total deposits and total advances increasing by 10% and 8%, respectively. The yield on assets increased by 7 basis points to 8.99%, while the cost of funds rose by 21 basis points to 5.46%. The net interest margin (NIM) declined by 9 basis points to 3.98% due to the increase in cost of funds. Overall, the bank's financial performance indicates a stable earnings profile, with core income streams constituting 97% of operating revenue.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health of Axis Bank appears to be stable, with a focus on managing employee benefit obligations. As of 31 March 2025, the present value of funded obligations for the gratuity benefit plan stood at ₹1,000.67 crore, while the fair value of plan assets was ₹955.00 crore, resulting in a net liability of ₹54.70 crore. This represents a decrease from the previous year's net liability of ₹102.30 crore. The bank has also made provisions for other employee benefits, including ₹3.70 crore for resettlement allowance and ₹0.19 crore for privilege leave liability.

In terms of cash flow, the bank has contributed ₹22.22 crore to the National Pension Scheme (NPS) for employees who have opted for the scheme, up from ₹15.54 crore in the previous year. The actual return on plan assets for the gratuity benefit plan was ₹66.57 crore, compared to an expected return of ₹52.69 crore. While the filing excerpts do not provide a comprehensive picture of the bank's cash flow position, the available data suggests that Axis Bank is managing its employee benefit obligations and making necessary provisions to ensure a stable balance sheet. However, a more detailed analysis of the bank's cash flow statement would be required to make a comprehensive assessment of its balance sheet health and cash flow position.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of Axis Bank has provided commentary on the bank's derivative transactions, which are undertaken for balance sheet management and proprietary trading. The bank has a functional separation between the Treasury Front Office, Treasury Mid Office, and Treasury Back Office to manage these transactions. The Market Risk Group independently identifies, measures, and monitors market risks associated with derivative transactions, and the Treasury Back Office undertakes activities such as trade validation, confirmation, settlement, and accounting. The bank has implemented policies on customer suitability and appropriateness to ensure that derivatives transactions are suitable for customers. The bank's gross PV01 position arising out of all non-option rupee derivative contracts is within 0.25% of its net worth as of the balance sheet date.

The bank's management has also provided information on its subsidiaries and associates, with Axis Bank Limited being the parent entity. As of March 31, 2024, the parent entity had net assets of ₹150,235 crore, accounting for 96.22% of the consolidated net assets. The bank's subsidiaries, including Axis Capital Limited, Axis Trustee Services Limited, and Axis Asset Management Company Limited, also reported net assets and profits for the year ended March 31, 2024. The bank has also reported contingent liabilities, including claims against the group not acknowledged as debts, with a provision of ₹904.76 crore as of March 31, 2025, towards claims assessed as probable. Overall, the management's commentary provides insight into the bank's risk management practices and financial performance.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks associated with AXISBANK's operations are primarily related to its derivative transactions. The Bank undertakes various derivative transactions, including Over the Counter (OTC) and Exchange Traded derivative transactions, which expose it to credit, market, legal, reputation, and operational risks. The Bank has implemented a risk management framework to mitigate these risks, including setting up risk limits for parameters such as PV01, VaR, Stop Loss, Delta, Gamma, and Vega. Additionally, the Bank ensures that the Gross PV01 position arising out of all non-option rupee derivative contracts are within 0.25% of its net worth as on the Balance Sheet date.

The Bank's derivative transactions are also subject to regulatory risks, as they are governed by the extant RBI guidelines. Furthermore, the Bank's forward-looking statements are subject to risks, uncertainties, and external factors, which may cause actual results to differ materially from projections. The Bank has identified material issues, including risk management, corporate governance, and regulatory compliance, which are guided by its integrated reporting framework. However, without additional information on the Bank's financial performance and peer comparison data, it is challenging to assess the magnitude of these risks.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The 'Bull vs Bear vs Base Case' scenario for Axis Bank is shaped by its derivative transactions and risk management framework. On the bull case, the bank's ability to manage risks associated with derivative transactions, as evident from its functional separation between Treasury Front Office, Treasury Mid Office, and Treasury Back Office, could lead to increased confidence among investors and customers. The bank's implementation of policies such as the Derivative policy, Suitability and Appropriateness Policy, and Market Risk Management policy, as well as its adherence to RBI guidelines, demonstrates a robust risk management framework. This could potentially lead to increased profitability and growth for the bank.

On the bear case, the bank's exposure to various risks, including credit, market, legal, reputation, and operational risk, associated with derivative transactions, could lead to significant losses if not managed effectively. The bank's Gross PV01 position, which is required to be within 0.25% of its net worth, is a key metric to watch. However, without specific numbers on the bank's current net worth and Gross PV01 position, it is difficult to assess the bank's risk exposure. As a base case, we assume that the bank will continue to manage its derivative transactions and associated risks effectively, given its established risk management framework and policies in place. Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 392 Derivatives are financial instruments whose characteristics are derived from an underlying asset, or from interest and exchange rates or indices. The Bank undertakes Over the Counter (OTC) and Exchange Traded derivative transactions for Balance Sheet management and also for proprietary trading/market making whereby the Bank offers OTC derivative products to the customers to enable them to hedge their interest rate and currency risks within the prevalent regulatory guidelines. Proprietary trading includes Exchange Traded Currency Options, Interest Rate Futures, Currency Futures and Rupee Interest Rate Swaps under different benchmarks (viz. MIBOR, Modified MIFOR, LIBOR, ARR and INBMK), Currency Options, Currency Swaps and Non Deliverable derivatives. The Bank also undertakes transactions in Cross Currency Swaps, Principal Only Swaps, Coupon Only Swaps, Currency Options, Interest Rate Swaps, Exotic Derivatives and Long Term Forex Contracts (LTFX) for hedging its Balance Sheet and also offers them to its customers. These transactions expose the Bank to various risks, primarily credit, market, legal, reputation and operational risk. The Bank has adopted the following mechanism for managing risks arising out of the derivative transactions. There is a functional separation between the Treasury Front Office, Treasury Mid Office and Treasury Back Office to undertake derivative transactions. The customer and interbank related derivative transactions are originated by Derivative sales and Treasury Front Office team respectively which ensures compliance with the trade origination requirements as per the Bank’s policy and the RBI guidelines. The Market Risk Group within the Bank’s Risk Department independently identifies, measures and monitors the market risks associated with derivative transactions and apprises the Asset Liability Management Committee (ALCO) and the Risk Management Committee of the Board (RMC) on the compliance with the risk limits. The Treasury Back Office undertakes activities such as trade validation, confirmation, settlement, ISDA and related documentation, post deal documentation, accounting, valuation and other MIS reporting. The derivative transactions are governed by the Derivative policy, Suitability and Appropriateness Policy for derivative products, Market Risk Management policy, Hedging policy and the Asset Liability Management (ALM) policy of the Bank as well as by the extant RBI guidelines. The Bank has implemented policy on customer suitability & appropriateness to ensure that derivatives transactions entered into are appropriate and suitable to the customer. The Bank has put in place a detailed process flow on documentation for customer derivative transactions for effective management of operational/reputation/compliance risk. Various risk limits are set up and actual exposures are monitored vis-à-vis the limits allocated. These limits are set up taking into account market volatility, risk appetite, business strategy and management experience. Risk limits are in place for risk parameters viz. PV01, VaR, Stop Loss, Delta, Gamma and Vega. Actual positions are monitored against these limits on a daily basis and breaches, if any, are dealt with in accordance with board approved Risk Appetite Statement. Risk assessment of the portfolio is undertaken periodically. The Bank ensures that the Gross PV01 (Price value of a basis point) position arising out of all non-option rupee derivative contracts are within 0.25% of net worth of the Bank as on Balance Sheet date.

Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 354 Valuation of Exchange Traded Currency Options (‘ETCO’) is carried out using internal pricing models and valuation of Interest Rate Futures (‘IRF’) is carried out on the basis of the daily settlement price of each contract provided by the exchange. Premium on options is recognized as income/expense on expiry or early termination of the transaction. Hedging derivatives including funding swaps Foreign exchange forward contracts not intended for trading (including funding swaps), that are entered into to establish the amount of reporting currency required or available at the settlement date of a transaction, and are outstanding at the Balance Sheet date, are effectively valued at the closing spot rate. The premium or discount arising at the inception of such forward exchange contract is amortised on a straight line basis as expense or income over the life of the contract. For hedge transactions through other derivatives, the Bank identifies the hedged item (asset or liability) at the inception of transaction itself. The effectiveness is ascertained at the time of inception of the hedge and periodically thereafter. In case of a fair value hedge, the changes in the fair value of the hedging instruments and hedged items are recognized in the Profit and Loss Account and in case of cash flow hedges, the change in fair value of hedging instrument for the effective portion is recognised in Schedule 2- ‘Reserves and Surplus’ under ‘Cash Flow Hedge Reserve’ and the ineffective portion of an effective hedging relationship, if any, is recognised in the Profit and Loss Account. The accumulated balance in the Cash Flow Hedge Reserve, in an effective hedging relationship, is recycled in the Profit and Loss Account at the same time that the impact from the hedged item is recognised in the Profit and Loss Account. Provisioning Pursuant to the RBI guidelines, any receivables under derivative contracts comprising of crystallised receivables as well as positive MTM in respect of future receivables which remain overdue for more than 90 days are reversed through the Profit and Loss account and are held in a separate suspense account under Schedule 5 – ‘Other Liabilities and Provisions’. 5.9 Revenue recognition Interest income is recognised on an accrual basis in accordance with AS–9, Revenue Recognition as notified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read together with the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021 and the RBI guidelines, except in the case of interest income on non-performing assets where it is recognised on receipt basis as per the income recognition and asset classification norms of RBI. Any discount or premium on the investments in debt-securities is amortised as interest income over the remaining life of the instrument. Interest income on investments in PTCs is recognized on a constant yield basis. Commission on Guarantees and Letters of Credit (‘LC’) is recognized on a pro-rata basis over the period of the Guarantee/ LC.
